subject: FinPay — VPC connectivity & integration follow-up

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: FinPay — VPC connectivity & integration follow-up

Hi Samir — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum on the POC: 

Recap:
- Goal: integrate Redwood hosted inference into FinPay's transaction enrichment pipeline with private connectivity (VPC endpoints / IP allowlist + mTLS).
- Primary concerns you raised: static egress IPs for allowlist, mutual TLS for server-auth and client certs, DNS resolution for our private endpoints, and routing via your GCP VPC.
- Expected initial traffic: ~50 TPS peak during batch windows, ~200k tokens/day, models will be mid-sized (7B) for NLU & reranking.

Open questions for your team (please confirm):
1) Will FinPay be able to establish a VPC Service Control / Private Service Connect to point to Redwood Private endpoints, or do you require public egress + IP allowlist?
2) Do you require Greenwood (sic) to present a client certificate, or do you prefer FinPay to use mTLS with supplied CA and have Redwood verify client certs?
3) Do you need DNS entries inside your VPC (private zones) pointing to Redwood endpoints, or is IP-based allowlisting sufficient?
4) Any procurement or SOC2 evidence we should include in the next packet?

Next steps I propose:
- I attached our integration checklist (redwood-integration-checklist.pdf) — fills in SDK/auth examples and networking patterns.
- If you confirm public egress + static IPs are acceptable, we can give a list of outbound IP ranges to allowlist. If you prefer private endpoints, we’ll schedule a technical dive with Jonas to map routing details.
- Technical dive: suggest Tue Feb 17, 10am PT — Jonas + Laura + me.

If you can reply with the answers to the questions above and confirm a time, we’ll lock in the POC plan.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference

From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@finpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@finpay.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:25:00 -0500
Subject: Re: FinPay — VPC connectivity & integration follow-up

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Short answers below; attaching our completed security questionnaire.

Answers:
1) We prefer private connectivity but are open to public egress with static IPs if the private option requires too much infra lead time. Our security team will push for Private Service Connect first.
2) We require mutual TLS. FinPay will act as the client initiating mTLS to Redwood’s endpoint. We can provide client certs signed by our internal CA; Redwood will need to validate those certs.
3) DNS inside our VPC is preferred (Private DNS zone) so we can point redwood-api.finpay.internal to the private endpoint.
4) Procurement: we need SOC2 Type II artifact, encryption-at-rest confirmation, and a data processing addendum.

Traffic/scale: initial POC targets 30–60 TPS; long-term could grow to 200 TPS. Latency sensitivity: p50 < 80ms for inference path.

Attachment: security_questionnaire_filled.pdf

We can do Tue Feb 17 10am PT for the technical dive — that works for our infra lead (Aisha) and me.

—Samir
Samir Gupta
Head of Engineering | FinPay

Subject: Re: FinPay — VPC connectivity & integration follow-up

Hi Samir — quick technical note ahead of the dive on Feb 17. High-level options and our recommendations: 

Option A — Private Service Connect / Private Endpoints (recommended):
- Redwood exposes a private endpoint reachable from your VPC. FinPay configures a Private Service Connect (or AWS PrivateLink equivalent) to connect.
- DNS: we can provide a CNAME or IP that your private zone maps to; recommended to use a private DNS entry (redwood-api.finpay.internal).
- mTLS: Redwood will accept client certs; we support configuring an accepted CA bundle. We can validate client certs against your CA or use a short-lived certting exchange (ACME-style) if you prefer.
- Egress: none required from your VPC to public internet for inference traffic.

Option B — Public egress + static IP allowlist (fastest to pilot):
- Redwood will provide a small set of stable outbound IP ranges you can allowlist.
- mTLS: still supported — Redwood can validate client certs presented over TLS to our public endpoint.
- DNS: not required but we can provide a canonical FQDN to use in your DNS.

Action items for the tech dive:
- We’ll share the Redwood outbound IP block list (if you choose option B) and the CA bundle instructions (if option A).
- Please bring a network diagram of FinPay’s VPC egress and any proxy/NAT appliances.
- We’ll demo SDK auth flows (API key + optional signed assertions for short-lived tokens) and show embedding/reranker integration patterns.

Pre-read links: 
- Networking guide: https://docs.redwood.com/networking/vpc-endpoints
- mTLS guide: https://docs.redwood.com/security/mtls

I’ll draft the short IP block list and CA config doc and drop it in the Drive before the meeting.

Jonas Weber
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
